issues: No integrity problems found. The diff only changes has_ve() so that every layer gets a value embedding instead of alternating layers. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. has_ve now ignores its arguments, but it is still used correctly. Giving every layer a value embedding adds embedding parameters and memory, which costs some VRAM and step throughput inside the fixed 300 s. That affects performance, not validity.

I couldn't recompute z independently. The candidate is 1.1122 against an incumbent mean of 1.1075, so it is 0.0047 worse. The reported z = -0.697 implies a spread of about 0.0067, but the incumbent's per-run values or standard deviation weren't provided, so I can't check that. The sign matches the convention that negative means worse.

The provisional reject agrees with the numbers: the single candidate run is worse than the incumbent mean. There is only one candidate run, so the evidence is weak either way, but there's no sign of improvement that would justify a replicate.
